mainEntity.name: What are the differences between indoor cycling and regular gym bikes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Indoor cycling classes, often called 'Spin' or 'cycle,' use specialized stationary bikes that allow for a wider range of motion and resistance adjustments, mimicking road cycling more closely. They typically involve an instructor-led group class with music and varied terrains. Regular gym bikes (recumbent or upright) are often self-paced and provide basic cardio workouts with fewer dynamic movements. At Cave Training, our indoor cycling classes offer a dynamic, engaging, and motivating group experience with expert coaching, which provides a significantly more challenging and structured workout than simply pedaling on a standard gym bike.
acceptedAnswer.description: Indoor cycling uses specialized bikes in instructor-led group classes with varied terrains, offering a more dynamic and challenging workout than basic self-paced gym bikes.
